text:
jordan_cs: Hi team — customer (AcmeCorp) reports a sudden spike in 429s this morning. They say most requests come from eu-west-1 clients but their usage/billing shows a lot of traffic billed to us-west-1. They attached a curl repro. Can we triage?

maya_support: thanks @jordan_cs. can you paste the raw response headers + request-id from one of the failing calls? 429 body would help too.

jordan_cs: pasted below (customer removed PII):

curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Response (HEADERS):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: req_20270312_abc123
x-region: us-west-1
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 35
content-type: application/json

Response body:
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","details":"region_quota_exhausted"}

jordan_cs: customer insists their network is EU and they set X-Redwood-Client-Region: eu-west-1 on some calls. They also said this started after their rollout at 08:12 UTC.

alex_oncall: looking at infra logs for req_20270312_abc123 ... I see an entry in the routing service: fallback-route triggered at 08:12:37 UTC -> target us-west-1 due to regional capacity headroom < 5%. There are also several overflow events matching their org id in eu-west-1 between 08:11 and 08:13.

alex_oncall: quick summary: eu-west-1 hit soft quota, routing policy "regional-preferred" allowed overflow to other regions. Billing attribution uses final serving region (us-west-1) so customer sees tokens billed there.

maya_support: is that expected behavior? customer thought we would queue or return 429 for cross-region attempts instead of routing out of region.

ryan_pm: this is working as designed for the default policy — we prefer latency but avoid hard throttles by overflow. But we should be explicit in docs and customer-facing error messages. Also need to check if this org had burst credits.

sana_ml: checking quota state for AcmeCorp org_9876: they had 0 burst credits left after a sudden spike from one service. quota history shows steady usage then a 20k token spike at 08:11:50. That matches their rollout window.

jordan_cs: customer wants a reproducible minimal test to show routing behavior. suggested steps from me: 1) set X-Redwood-Client-Region: eu-west-1, 2) send a tight burst of N requests in < 10s, 3) watch x-region and x-rate-limit-* headers.

alex_oncall: here's an internal repro script we used (safe to share):

```
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{stdout}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_xxx" \
    -H "X-Redwood-Client-Region: eu-west-1" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"load test"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
  sleep 0.12
done
wait
```

alex_oncall: watch the x-region response header. if you see us-west-1 then overflow occured. also look for header x-fallback-reason: region_quota_exhausted or crosszone_fallback.

maya_support: noted. Jordan, please send that to the customer and ask for one failed request's raw headers so we can correlate.

jordan_cs: sent. they replied with two failing entries and one served in-eu. Here are their three request-ids: req_20270312_abc123, req_20270312_def456, req_20270312_ghi789.

alex_oncall: correlated those: abc123 and def456 -> routed to us-west-1 (fallback), ghi789 -> served in eu-west-1. The routing log shows a brief window where eu-west queued but then drained and allowed some local serves. No infrastructure errors.

ryan_pm: product question: do we want default behavior to overflow or prefer hard regional reject? This customer expected hard per-region quotas. If we change default, we'd increase latency and user-visible 429s.

sana_ml: also important: billing visibility. For customers doing compliance/regional controls, billing attribution by final-serving-region can be confusing. We should expose x-billed-region or an opt-in account setting to pin billing to preferred region and return 429 if that can't be honored.

jordan_cs: customer asked for short-term mitigations. I've suggested: 1) pin region header on their requests (X-Redwood-Client-Region + org-level setting), 2) enable strict-region routing in console (if on Dedicated/Private) or request feature flag for Hosted, 3) request temporary increase to eu-west-1 reserved capacity OR purchase burst credits.

maya_support: I opened a billing note: linked to org_9876's account invoice team and flagged possible cost-impact. Also created an internal ticket INT-8721 to review region billing attribution docs.

deploy-bot: routing-policy v1.3.7 canary deployed to routing-service at 08:30 UTC (:rocket:)

alex_oncall: follow-up action items:
- confirm if AcmeCorp wants strict regional rejection or prefers overflow (jordan to confirm)
- ops to evaluate temporary eu-west-1 capacity bump (maya + infra)
- docs/product to add clarity about billing attribution and opt-in region pinning (ryan + sana)

jordan_cs: customer replied — they want strict region enforcement (they can't have data leave EU) and will accept higher latency / retries. I told them we'll escalate.

maya_support: escalated to infra for immediate change: request strict-region flag for org_9876 on hosted control plane. infra please advise ETA.

alex_oncall: infra notes: we can flip a per-org routing policy for hosted customers that causes region mismatch -> immediate 429. This is a control-plane change and requires a config push and short rolling restart of router pods. ETA ~45m during which new requests will follow new policy. No data plane change.

sana_ml: logged PR to add account-level flag and UI copy. Also adding a telemetry metric to show number of overflowed requests per org per day.

jordan_cs: I'll communicate ETA to AcmeCorp and include repro script and recommended settings. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maya_support: closing loop: once infra flips the flag, ask the customer to retest with the same minimal script and paste headers if they still see cross-region serves. we'll reopen if needed.

alex_oncall: note for postmortem: consider adding a billing field to API responses: x-billed-region and an admin audit log entry when overflowed to different region. Saves a lot of back-and-forth.

jordan_cs: logged customer case CS-4312 and linked INT-8721. will update thread when infra confirms change.

maya_support: thanks — marking this thread as monitoring.
